newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHOCK DEFEAT PUTS RANGERS TITLE BID ON HOLD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOCK DEFEAT PUTS RANGERS TITLE BID ON HOLD.

text.p: Rangers blew a golden chance to seal a record-equalling ninth consecutive Scottish championship on Monday when relegation-threatened Motherwell shocked the Glasgow giants 2-0 at Ibrox.
Walter Smith's side needed just one point to take the title and equal arch-rival Celtic's title-winning run from 1966 to 1974.
A double strike by Owen Coyle secured the win for Motherwell and Rangers must now gain the point they need from a visit to Dundee United on Wednesday or at Hearts on Saturday.
Rangers started apprehensively and after just seven minutes Coyle had silenced the partisan Ibrox crowd.
Ian Ross knocked the ball square and Coyle swept his left foot shot beyond goalkeeper Andy Dibble.
The underdogs almost extended their lead just 60 seconds later when Shaun McSkimming attempted a chip from 20 metres out which Dibble did well to tip over the bar.
The home side looked nervous and unimaginative and shortly before halftime the crowd was shouting for substitute Paul Gascoigne to come on.
The appearance of the England midfielder for the second half was greeted by roars of approval but Gascoigne's contribution proved a disappointment.

Wave after wave of Rangers attacks were soaked up by the Motherwell defence. Gascoigne missed Rangers' best chance on the hour when, clear through on goal, he poked his shot past goalkeeper Scott Howie but wide of the post.
The Ibrox faithful were stunned when Motherwell made sure of the win through a Coyle penalty seven minutes from time after a clumsy Ian Durrant challenge on Micky Weir in the box.

The dejected Rangers players were booed off at the end and it was a sad Ibrox farewell for captain Richard Gough who leaves for Kansas City Wizards in the U.S. Major Soccer League at the end of this season.
